chart.title: Delhi’s 2024: the summer that would not break
chart.note: May and June ran above the normal range for weeks, and the nights stayed hot.
chart.geography: New Delhi (28.6° N, 77.2° E; ERA5 grid cell)

sources.maker: ECMWF Copernicus Climate Change Service (ERA5 reanalysis)
sources.dataset: Open-Meteo Historical Weather API, daily 2 m temperature maximum and minimum

chart.method: Normal range: the average daily low and high on each calendar day over 1991–2020, rounded to 0.1. 29 February is averaged over the leap years in that range. Records: the lowest low and highest high on each calendar day from 1940 to 2024; a marked day of 2024 set or equalled its record.

chart.title: Every year since 1850, as a stripe
chart.note: Each stripe is one year of the world's average temperature. The last red decade is not a blip.

chart.title: Every day of 2024 in Delhi, against its normal
chart.note: Every day of January ran below its normal. May and June ran above it on about five days in six.
chart.geography: New Delhi (ERA5 grid cell at 28.6° N, 77.2° E)

sources.dataset: ERA5 reanalysis, daily maximum and minimum temperature at 2 m

chart.method: Each day’s high minus the average high on that calendar day over 1991–2020 (the normal, rounded to 0.1 °C), for 29 February over the leap years in that range only.
